podcast.body: For years, Randy California of Spirit and later his estate claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off the guitar arpeggio from Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for this song. The contentious court case spanned years, delving into complex musical theory and copyright law, and reached the Supreme Court in 2020. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled against the plagiarism claims, stating there should be no more talk of it being a rip-off. "Suffices to say that after trial after trial, the case reached on appeal all the way to the Supreme Court in 2020. But after looking at all the details, the court said, get out of here. There should be no more talk of Stairway to Heaven being a rip off of Taras."

podcast.body: This song is analytically described as a "bombastic fusion of guitar-driven rock and roll, psychedelia, art rock, and folk music." It integrates English and Celtic mythology, delving into folk mysticism with allusions to the "make queen" and "piper." According to Larry Star and Christopher Waterman, the song exemplifies the "twin musical threads of sonic aggression and acoustic intimacy," creating a "sacred experience." It was famously never released as a single, necessitating album purchase. Persistent rumors of backward satanic messages are dismissed as conspiracy theories, and live performances of the song are lauded as an "incredible experience."
